ustav.title: Ustav Crne Gore (Službeni list Crne Gore, br. 1/2007)
ustav.note: Adopted 19 October 2007. Arts. 82-84 (Skupština, deputies elected directly, four-year term), 95-97 (President elected directly for five years, at most twice), 113-118 (local self-government), 154 (Constitutional Court judges elected by the Skupština), 157 (referendum on amending core articles). Amended 2013 (Amendments I-XVI) and 2026 (Amendments XVII-XXI, judiciary).

ustav_1992.title: Ustav Republike Crne Gore (Službeni list Republike Crne Gore, br. 48/1992)
ustav_1992.note: Constitution of 12 October 1992 for the Republic of Montenegro within the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; replaced by the 2007 Constitution.

zakon_izbori.title: Zakon o izboru odbornika i poslanika (prečišćeni tekst)
zakon_izbori.note: Law of 1998 (Sl. list RCG 4/98) consolidated through Sl. list CG 114/26. Arts. 3 (30 councillors plus one per 5,000 voters), 4-5 (party lists; four-year term), 12 (each municipality and the whole country one constituency), 13-13b (general local elections in all municipalities every fourth year on the second Sunday in June; deputies' elections called by the President), 94-95 (3% threshold, minority exceptions at 0.7% and 0.35% for Croat lists, D'Hondt), 120b (first general local elections 13 June 2027). The 2025 amendments renamed the State Election Commission the Central Election Commission.

zakon_predsjednik.title: Zakon o izboru predsjednika Crne Gore (prečišćeni tekst)
zakon_predsjednik.note: Sl. list CG 17/07, 8/09, 12/16, 73/18. Arts. 1 (direct election, five-year term), 2 (called by the Speaker at least 120 days before the term ends), 16-17 (majority of valid votes of those who voted; otherwise a second round of the top two 14 days later).

zakon_predsjednik_1992.title: Zakon o izboru predsjednika Republike (Službeni list Republike Crne Gore, br. 49/1992)
zakon_predsjednik_1992.note: Presidential election law of 1992; election valid only if more than half the registered voters took part (art. 16), the rule that voided the votes of December 2002 and February 2003. Replaced by the law of Sl. list RCG 11/2003.

zakon_predsjednik_opstine.title: Zakon o izboru predsjednika opštine (Službeni list Republike Crne Gore, br. 42/2003)
zakon_predsjednik_opstine.note: Published 16 July 2003. Art. 1 (mayor elected by citizens directly and by secret ballot), 2 (five-year term), 4 (called by the municipal assembly), 22-23 (majority of valid votes, otherwise a second round of the top two 14 days later).

zls_2018.title: Zakon o lokalnoj samoupravi (Službeni list Crne Gore, br. 2/2018)
zls_2018.note: Local self-government law of 2018: municipal assembly elected directly, mayor elected by the assembly; local communities (mjesne zajednice) set up by municipal decision.

zls_2026.title: Zakon o lokalnoj samoupravi (Službeni list Crne Gore, br. 133/2026)
zls_2026.note: Adopted 4 September 2026, published 11 September 2026, applied from 13 June 2027. Art. 2 (units: opština, grad, Glavni grad, Prijestonica; mjesna zajednica and gradska opština as sub-units), 51 (assembly elected directly), 72-73 (the assembly elects the mayor from the list leaders and candidates of the last local elections, for four years).

zto_2011.title: Zakon o teritorijalnoj organizaciji Crne Gore (Službeni list Crne Gore, br. 54/2011)
zto_2011.note: Published 17 November 2011. Art. 5 (Glavni grad Podgorica, with the urban municipalities Golubovci and Tuzi), 6 (Prijestonica Cetinje), 7 (19 municipalities: Andrijevica, Bar, Berane, Bijelo Polje, Budva, Danilovgrad, Žabljak, Kotor, Kolašin, Mojkovac, Nikšić, Plav, Plužine, Pljevlja, Rožaje, Tivat, Ulcinj, Herceg Novi, Šavnik).

classes.note: Two-round majority: a candidate needs more than half the valid votes, otherwise the top two meet 14 days later. Under the 1992 law an election was valid only if more than half the registered voters took part, which voided the votes of 22 December 2002 and 9 February 2003. In 1990 voters elected the President of the Presidency of the Socialist Republic.

classes.name: Neposredni izbori za predsjednika opštine
classes.finest_note: Only the municipal commissions' reports in the gazette, by municipality.
classes.note: From the 2003 law, voters elected mayors for five years by two-round majority, usually with the assembly; the amendments of December 2009 (in force 8 January 2010) gave the choice back to the assembly. Kotor's election of 8 November 2009 was among the last.

cadence.runoff_rule: More than half the valid votes; otherwise the top two meet 14 days later (Zakon o izboru predsjednika opštine arts. 22-23).

access.format: html (page images of the printed gazette)
access.evidence: Calling decisions and municipal commissions' reports for direct mayoral elections.

classes.name: Opštinski i mjesni referendumi
classes.note: Municipal assemblies call municipal referendums, binding or consultative, and local-community referendums for part of their territory (Zakon o referendumu; Zakon o lokalnoj samoupravi). Run by a commission each assembly appoints; results appear in the gazette. Consultative referendums preceded the creation of Petnjica (2012) and Gusinje (2013); one for Tuzi was called and withdrawn in 2010.

access.evidence: Commission reports for Petnjica 2012, Gusinje 2013, and Zeta (Botun) 2025.

classes.name: Izbori za Skupštinu Narodne (Socijalističke) Republike Crne Gore
classes.disposition_reason: Single-list and delegate-system elections from the Constituent Assembly to 1986; results were published only in the printed Službeni list NRCG/SRCG, whose online register starts in 1992, and no official online copy was found.

classes.name: Izbori za Crnogorsku narodnu skupštinu
classes.name_en: National Assembly of the Principality and Kingdom, 1905-1914
classes.disposition_reason: Elections under the 1905 Constitution (first session 1906, last election 1914) were reported only in the period's official gazette and Assembly records held by the State Archives; no official online copy of the results was found.

classes.name: Savezni izbori (SFRJ, SRJ, Srbija i Crna Gora)
classes.disposition_reason: Elections to the Yugoslav federal assemblies, the 2000 federal presidency, and the Assembly of Serbia and Montenegro (chosen by the republic parliaments in 2003) belong to the federal polity's census, not Montenegro's.

classes.name: Izbori za savjete manjinskih naroda
classes.disposition_reason: Each council is made up of ex officio members (deputies, councillors, and other officials of the minority) and members chosen at an electoral assembly of electors who each gathered 30 to 100 signatures; no electorate votes and the election commissions do not run them.

classes.name: Izbor savjeta mjesnih zajednica
classes.disposition_reason: Each municipality sets how local-community councils are chosen in its own decision (citizens' meetings or local ballots run by the municipality); the election commissions do not run them and no register of results exists.

classes.name: Posredni izbori
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by elected bodies: the Prime Minister and Government and the Speaker by the Skupština; the President of the Presidency's members in 1990-1992; mayors by the municipal assembly before 2004 and since 2010 (Zakon o lokalnoj samoupravi 2018 and 2026); assembly chairs; the Ombudsman. No electorate votes.

classes.name: Izbor sudija i tužilaca
classes.disposition_reason: Judges are appointed by the Judicial Council and Constitutional Court judges elected by the Skupština on nominations of the President and the Skupština (Ustav arts. 127-128, 154); no judge is elected by voters.

classes.name: Stranački unutrašnji izbori
classes.disposition_reason: Parties and groups of voters nominate lists and candidates under their own statutes; the law provides no state-run primary and the commissions publish no such votes.
